sentences: A wave64 VS/PS/GS on a 32-wide subgroup is exact **iff its observable results do not change when the wave is cut into two 32-lane halves** (the host forms the subgroups of graphics stages, so there is no partner half to exchange with).

`tools/wave64_halves.py` decides it from the code (forward taint dataflow over the basic blocks, plus control dependence on wave-wide votes) and the translator records it in `index.json` as `wave64_graphics` (`A`/`B`/`C`), `wave64_graphics_reasons` (tier C) and `wave64_graphics_idioms` (tier B).

**A**: only per-lane arithmetic, votes that skip lane-masked work (`s_cbranch_execz/execnz`; `vccz/vccnz` whose run side starts by narrowing EXEC to that VCC and whose other side is the join, with no code of its own: a half that votes no runs that side, the wave does not; the same holds for `s_cbranch_execz/execnz`: the side that runs when EXEC is zero is taken by a half with no active lane, so it must be the join (or only jumps to it) or the exit of a loop the vote closes, else tier C `unsafe-execz-branch`; `s_cbranch_scc*` after a vote is the same kind of skip, any other reader of that SCC, `s_cselect`/`s_cmov`/`s_addc`, is tier C), whole-quad masks, `ds_bpermute`/`ds_permute`/`v_permlane16`/`v_permlanex16`/`ds_swizzle` (they stay inside a half), a `ds_bpermute`/`ds_permute` address made from the lane id (`v_mbcnt_lo` then `v_mbcnt_hi` of -1) when it is the same modulo 128 bytes in the wave and in a half (the id is 0..63 there and 0..31 here, equal modulo 32 lanes; sums, differences and bitwise ops with invariant values keep that, a left shift by c multiplies the modulus by 2^c, and the permute uses address bits 2..6 of its half only: `(id ^ 1) << 2` is exact, `id << 1`, a right shift of the id or the low count alone stay tier C `lane-id`), loops closed by `execnz` with no scalar state carried.

`s_cbranch_scc*` after a vote is the same kind of skip, any other reader of that SCC, `s_cselect`/`s_cmov`/`s_addc`, is tier C), whole-quad masks, `ds_bpermute`/`v_permlane16` (they stay inside a half, not GPU-tested here: no fixture; `ds_swizzle` and `v_permlanex16` likewise), loops closed by `execnz` with no scalar state carried.

**B**: also a waterfall loop (`v_readfirstlane` of a varying value, `v_cmp_eq` against the same VGPR, `saveexec`, body, `s_xor exec`, `execnz`; the scalar only used inside the body), a wave-aggregated atomic (`s_bcnt1` of EXEC, `v_mbcnt` rank of that same EXEC, one `buffer_atomic_add` of that count (the count of the mask the rank ranks) by the rank-0 lane only, `v_readfirstlane` of the result with EXEC restored, base + rank as a store address, the rank counting the very mask the atomic's count was taken of (a rank of the entry EXEC or of a saved copy next to a base of the narrowed one is tier C `lane-rank`); the rank alone or the base alone is not a slot: exact as a set of slots, **the order of the slots within a wave is not preserved**, a 64-lane wave takes one run of slots, two halves take two), `v_readfirstlane` / `v_readlane` of a VGPR written from scalars and constants while EXEC was the launch mask (the same in every lane), a `v_writelane` / `v_readlane` spill pair on one constant lane below 32.

**C**: anything else that reaches an export, a store's data, a branch or EXEC: lane count / rank / first-lane index / raw lane id (`v_mbcnt` of -1), `v_readlane` of a varying value at any lane (on a wave64 every lane gets hardware lane N, in halves each half gets its own lane N, so lane 7 is as wrong as lane 40; the research note's row 9 is too generous here); an analysis failure is tier C with reason `analysis-error` (the translation does not fail), `v_writelane` to a non-constant or >= 32 lane, a 32-bit access to half of a lane mask (`exec_hi`, `vcc_hi`, a mask pair's odd register), a mask read as data (including a mask combined by `s_and/or/andn2_b64` with a register that is not one: a user value, a loaded mask), a scalar defined behind a wave-wide vote and read where it may not have run (`s_add s5, s5, 1` after `s_cbranch_vccz`; a trip count in an SGPR of a divergent loop: the halves vote differently), a branch on a count, an elected-lane side effect that is not a count, `ds_append`/`ds_consume`.
The check is conservative: unknown means C.

`--wave64-graphics=warn` (default) marks tier C and counts it in the summary line, `error` refuses it (`Unsupported`), `off` skips the analysis; `python tools/wave64_halves.py --census <spirv>/index.json` prints tier, reason and idiom counts (no names); it complements `tools/wave64_graphics_scan.py` (#1132), which counts candidate cross-half opcodes in the disassembly before translation and decides nothing.

**Corpus census** (TEST-319, 1.0.2.1, `--census` over the translated index, re-run with the GS ring rule below and #1982): 11,405 wave64 graphics shaders (1,179 VS, 10,031 PS, 195 GS); tier A 2,117 (18.6%), B 17 (0.1%), C 9,271 (81.3%): VS 479/14/686, PS 1,443/3/8,585, GS 195/0/0.

Tier C reasons (a shader can have several): unsafe-vote-branch 8,285, tainted-branch 6,550, tainted-exec 5,189, cross-lane 4,760, stale-scalar 3,415, mask-half 758, unsafe-execz-branch 583, first-lane 353, waterfall-scalar 161, lane-id 152, lane-count 1. 11,405 wave64 graphics shaders (1,179 VS, 10,031 PS, 195 GS); tier A 1,919 (16.8%), B 17 (0.1%), C 9,469 (83.0%): VS 465/14/700, PS 1,454/3/8,574, GS 0/0/195.

Tier C reasons (a shader can have several): unsafe-vote-branch 8,175, tainted-branch 6,582, cross-lane 6,111, tainted-exec 4,959, stale-scalar 3,162, mask-half 758, unsafe-execz-branch 583, first-lane 353, lane-id 277, waterfall-scalar 167, lane-count 1.
Tier B idioms: readfirstlane-uniform 558, lane-spill 287, waterfall 35.
The lane-id bpermute rule moves no corpus shader.
**Corpus coverage is not measured here**: it needs a run over the game's shaders by someone who has them.

**Rewrite (the only one the emission needs)**: `v_readlane_b32` of a proven-uniform VGPR reads the lane's own copy instead of shuffling from lane N, because a subgroup shuffle from lane >= 32 of a 32-wide subgroup is undefined (143 of 144 test shaders translate byte-identically to origin/main, only `ps_w64_b_readlane_uniform` changed).

Everything else tier B needs is what the translator already emits per subgroup: the ballot/count/rank/first-lane words of `wave_mask` are the subgroup's own (the high word is 0), `v_readfirstlane` is the subgroup's first active lane, a waterfall runs once per distinct value of the subgroup.

GPU-checked on AMD Radeon 880M (driver 26.11.2; `requiredSubgroupSizeStages` has FRAGMENT, size 32..64) with `runtime/test/shaders/w64_graphics.py`: each `ps_w64_*` fixture drawn with the fragment subgroup size required to 64 (one hardware wave) and to 32 (two halves).

`ps_w64_a_skip`, `_b_waterfall`, `_b_readfirstlane`, `_b_readlane_uniform` and `_b_ballot_atomic` (counter 1024 and the 1024 slot words as a set; slot order differs) match each other and the words their headers derive; `_c_bcnt_export`, `_c_lane_id`, `_c_readlane`, `_c_vote_stale`, `_c_vote_else`, `_c_scc_vote`, `_c_execz_sgpr` (an SGPR written on the exec-zero side and exported) and `_c_waterfall_count` differ between 64 and 32 (the detector is right).

`ps_w64_a_one_lane` is the case where only one pixel votes yes (so one half votes and the other does not, in the wave and in the halves): its skip regions (`execz`, `vccz`, `vccnz` with a jump-only fall-through) give equal images at 64 and 32; `_c_vote_else` (code on the vote's no side) and `_c_scc_vote` (SCC of a vote as data) differ.

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop (32 only, driver 617.42): tier A/B fixtures equal the derived words and the 880M@64 images (`W64G_SAVE_REF` / `W64G_REF`), tier C fixtures differ from the 880M@64 images.

`ps_w64_a_permlane`, `_a_swizzle` and `_a_bpermute` (TEST-319: permlane16 neighbour selects, permlanex16 there and back, swizzle quad-permute, swap and broadcast modes, bpermute from lane-id addresses; every read stays in the pixel's 2x2 quad or comes back, so the words do not depend on how pixels are packed into lanes) give the derived words on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 (Linux, driver 620.73.04, 32 only).

With an AMD Radeon RX 580 (Polaris, RADV Mesa 26.0.8) as the 64-lane reference (`W64G_SAVE_REF`; GCN has one subgroup size, 64, in every stage but no FRAGMENT in `requiredSubgroupSizeStages`, so `vk_harness` counts a requested size equal to a device's only size as applied), the RTX 5070 run of every fixture (`W64G_REF`) equals the reference for all 13 tier A/B fixtures and differs from it for all 11 tier C ones, pixel and vertex; the same reads in a vertex shader run on the wave interpreter (64 lanes against two waves of 32, equal) because a GPU's partial vertex waves leave the lanes they would read empty.

Vertex shaders: the VS stage cannot be forced on the 880M (no VERTEX in `requiredSubgroupSizeStages`), so VS is covered by the strict wave interpreter (`tests/semantic/test_wave64_halves.py`: 64 lanes against two waves of 32; tier A/B equal, tier C differs); geometry shaders are not tested (the corpus ones are wave32; no fixture). 64 lanes against two waves of 32; tier A/B equal, tier C differs), and on RADV also on the GPU (TEST-251): RADV runs the VS stage (NGG) as wave64 by default and as wave32 with `RADV_PERFTEST=gewave32` (GFX10+, seen in the `RADV_DEBUG=shaders` dump: 64-bit EXEC operations against `exec_lo`), so `w64_graphics.py` draws each `vs_w64_*` fixture both ways, 960 zero-area vertices (`VKH_VERTICES`) that store four words each to the heap, with `vs_w64_c_lane_id` as the probe that the wave size changed (largest lane id 63, then 31).

RADV packs 62 or 64 vertices into a wave64 and 30 or 32 into a wave32, so the 32-lane run repacks the vertices rather than halving the waves; tier A/B words are keyed on the vertex index, which makes this the stricter test.

`vs_w64_a_skip`, `_b_waterfall`, `_b_readlane_uniform` (readfirstlane and readlane 40/63 of uniform VGPRs) and `_b_ballot_atomic` (240 slots as a set) give the derived words at both sizes; `_c_bcnt_export`, `_c_readlane` and `_c_lane_id` differ (the detector is right), on an RX 9070 XT (GFX1201) and a Ryzen 9800X3D iGPU (GFX1036, RDNA2), RADV Mesa 26.3.1; geometry shaders are not tested (no fixture; the corpus has 195 wave64 geometry shaders, all tier C, see the census).

`_c_bcnt_export`, `_c_readlane` and `_c_lane_id` differ (the detector is right), on an RX 9070 XT (GFX1201) and a Ryzen 9800X3D iGPU (GFX1036, RDNA2), RADV Mesa 26.3.1; geometry shaders likewise (TEST-251): RADV runs the GS stage (NGG) as wave64 by default and as wave32 with `gewave32`, and `w64_graphics.py` draws each `gs_w64_*` fixture after `vs_ids` (960 vertices, 320 triangles, `VKH_GS`), each invocation finding its triangle from `vs_ids`'s vertex number and storing four words to the heap, with `gs_w64_c_lane_id` as the probe (largest lane id 41, RADV puts at most 42 GS invocations in a wave64, then 31).

**LDS writes of a legacy GS:** `rdna2spirv.gs_ds` maps one to an output slot from its offset alone and drops the VGPR address (the lane's GSVS area), so `wave64_halves.py` checks only the data a GS `ds_write` writes, not its address; before, a lane id that only formed the GSVS base made the shader tier C `lane-id`.

Confirmed three ways: a hand-written GS with the base `lane id * 96` translates, after `spirv-opt -O`, to the same instructions as without it; `gs_w64_a_ring` (that shape) gives the derived records at wave64 and wave32 on both GPUs; and `tests/semantic/test_wave64_halves.py` (`GeometryRing`) keeps the lane id in the written data, or in a memory store's address, tier C.
The corpus GS form their GSVS base from `v_mbcnt_lo/hi` (all 195 contain `v_mbcnt_hi`): they were all a false tier C, and the census above has all 195 at tier A.
`wave64_halves.py --census` on a translated corpus shows it.

`_c_bcnt_export`, `_c_readlane` and `_c_lane_id` differ (the detector is right), on an RX 9070 XT (GFX1201) and a Ryzen 9800X3D iGPU (GFX1036, RDNA2), RADV Mesa 26.3.1; geometry shaders are not tested (the corpus ones are wave32; no fixture).
Not checked: helper lanes of partial quads; `VK_KHR_shader_maximal_reconvergence` is assumed for waterfall and election loops.

Tiers A and B assume subgroups of at least 32 lanes: a fragment stage may run fewer live lanes than the subgroup size it reports (Intel UHD 770: gl_SubgroupSize 32, ballot count 16, a shuffle from lane L^16 returns garbage; measured by kapitche, TEST-433), so `w64_graphics.py` skips the tier A/B pixel fixtures on a device whose minimum subgroup size is below 32 when neither the 64 nor the 32 run took effect; deriving the skip from a measured live fragment width (ballot count) in `vk_harness` is a follow-up.
